title: Laksa
subtitle: Malaysian coconut curry noodle soup with prawns
excerpt: Laksa is Malaysia's most famous noodle soup -- a rich, spiced coconut broth poured over rice noodles and topped with prawns. The paste is the heart of the dish, made from shallots, lemongrass, galangal, and dried chilli. It is a substantial, deeply flavoured soup that takes time but delivers something remarkable.
sourceNotes: Laksa is a dish of Peranakan origin, the culture of Chinese settlers who married into Malay communities in Malaysia and Singapore from the fifteenth century onward. The two main styles are Curry Laksa (coconut-based) and Assam Laksa (tamarind-based, from Penang). This recipe follows the coconut curry style most widely known internationally.

content.text: Laksa is a project of a dish -- the paste takes effort, but it is where all the flavour lives. Once the paste is made and fried, the rest comes together quickly. The broth should be rich and deeply spiced with a clear coconut sweetness underneath. Do not rush the paste stage.

items.prepNote: peeled and deveined -- reserve the shells for stock
use a 400ml tin of coconut milk
use 200g rice noodles or vermicelli -- soak and drain

content.text: Make the laksa paste. Roughly chop the shallots, garlic, ginger, and lemongrass. Blend with the turmeric and chilli flakes. Add a splash of oil and blend to a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Fry the laksa paste for 5 minutes, stirring, until fragrant and the oil separates from the paste.
Pour in the stock and bring to a simmer. Add the fish sauce. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk. Simmer gently for 10 more minutes. Do not boil hard.
Add the prawns. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until pink and cooked through.
Cook the noodles separately according to the packet. Drain. Place in deep bowls. Ladle the laksa broth and prawns over the noodles. Squeeze lime over. Top with spring onion. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Laksa paste is bitter or raw-tasting
items.fix: Fry the paste in oil for at least 5 minutes over medium heat, stirring constantly. The paste must lose its raw smell and turn a deeper colour before the liquid goes in. Under-fried paste dominates and overwhelms the soup.

content.text: Laksa is one of Malaysia's most celebrated dishes. It is a dish of mixed heritage -- Chinese noodle techniques combined with Malay spice pastes and coconut milk. In Penang, the tamarind-based assam laksa is considered one of the world's great soups. The coconut curry version is rich and warming. Each hawker centre stall has its own paste recipe.
